text:
For two periods this was a goaltenders' night, and Dustin Wolf was the reason Calgary was still ahead when it stopped being one. He made 29 saves, including a 25% look from Adrian Kempe in the second period, and finished as the first star. Yegor Sharangovich did the rest, scoring with 1:14 left to put the Flames up 3-1 and win it 3-2 in Los Angeles.

Morgan Frost opened the scoring 2:13 into the second off a Sharangovich feed, on a shot that goes in about 9% of the time. Joel Armia tied it 6:21 into the third, and Matvei Gridin answered five minutes later off a Martin Pospisil pass. That goal moved Calgary's win chance from 48% to 81%, and it made Gridin the player who added the most to the result by our measure. Mats Zuccarello scored 18 seconds after Sharangovich's goal, on a 2% chance, the least likely goal of the night, but there wasn't time for more.

The Kings have a case that they deserved better. They led in shot attempts 65-55 and in even-strength expected goals, the quality of chances, 2.46 to 1.98, and they won this game in 58% of our replays of every shot. Alex Laferriere had two assists and five shots. Anton Forsberg was solid at the other end (21 saves on 23 shots), and his best stop, on Joel Farabee in the third, kept it tied for a while. Neither power play scored in three tries.

For Los Angeles, it's four straight losses, and this one came with Artemi Panarin out for family reasons, per Daily Faceoff. Peter Laviolette's team has been out-played in spells and out-finished in others; tonight it was the second. For Calgary, it was a needed road win in a 2-2-1 week with Kevin Bahl gone for the season. The Flames go straight to Anaheim for the second half of a back-to-back.
headline: Sharangovich's late goal leaves the Kings winless in four
